title: Alfred Dillwyn Knox
name: Alfred Dillwyn Knox
summary: British classicist and cryptanalyst whose pre-war and wartime work helped establish Bletchley Park’s attack on Enigma.
whyThisMatters: Knox was a formative teacher and analyst in British cryptology. His work illustrates how linguistic, mathematical, and procedural reasoning combined in early attacks on machine ciphers.

sections.overview:
Alfred Dillwyn “Dilly” Knox was a British classicist and cryptanalyst. He worked for British codebreaking organizations in the First and Second World Wars and was among the early specialists examining Enigma at Bletchley Park.

Early Enigma work

Knox led research work that helped train and organize cryptanalysts during the opening phase of Bletchley Park. His team worked with insights from Polish cryptanalysis while pursuing additional methods against German traffic.

In memoriam

Knox died in 1943 while still connected to wartime cryptologic work. His influence survives in the people and methods he helped develop.
